title: Recharge Tariff for Damage, Cleaning, Tolls and Traffic Fines
content:
After a vehicle has been handed back, four heads of charge may be recharged to the renter, and a fifth
figure fixes how long the supplier has to report damage at all. Each of the six Car Rental Rate Classes
publishes its own tariff.

| Rate class | Damage reporting window, in calendar days | Damage administration charge, in USD | Administration on each toll, in USD | Administration on each traffic fine, in USD | Cleaning charge, in USD | Smoking charge, in USD |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pay Now Saver Rate | 14 | 125 | 9.95 | 49 | 150 | 400 |
| Pay Now Standard Rate | 14 | 110 | 9.95 | 45 | 140 | 375 |
| Pay At Counter Flex Rate | 10 | 95 | 8.95 | 39 | 125 | 350 |
| Inclusive Flex Rate | 7 | 75 | 6.95 | 29 | 110 | 325 |
| Premium Inclusive Rate | 5 | 0 | 0 | 25 | 95 | 300 |
| Corporate Negotiated Drive Rate | 10 | 65 | 5.95 | 25 | 110 | 325 |

## Reading the tariff

The reporting window is a length of time and not a charge: it is the calendar days a class allows the
supplier for reporting damage after the vehicle came back, and it runs from 5 days on the Premium
Inclusive Rate to 14 days on the two Pay Now classes.

The two administration columns are priced differently by their grain. Toll administration is published for
each toll recharged; fine administration is published for each fine. On the Premium Inclusive Rate toll
administration is nothing while fine administration is 25 USD, so the two heads do not move together.

The cleaning and smoking charges are figures for the whole rental. The cheapest tariff of the six is the
Premium Inclusive Rate at 95 USD and 300 USD; the dearest is the Pay Now Saver Rate at 150 USD and 400 USD.
The Inclusive Flex Rate and the Corporate Negotiated Drive Rate publish the same pair at 110 USD and 325 USD
while differing on every other column of the tariff.
